quizzes.title: Introduction to Electronic Components & Breadboarding
quizzes.subject: Electronics
quizzes.description: Unit 1 reviewer — resistors, capacitors, breadboards, circuits, LEDs, and jumper wires.

questions.q: What is the unit of resistance?
questions.explain: The ohm (Ω) is the unit of resistance.

questions.q: Which component limits or controls the flow of electric current in a circuit?
questions.explain: A resistor protects components like LEDs from too much current.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a resistor in a circuit?
Which type of resistor has a resistance value that CANNOT be adjusted?
Which type of resistor has an adjustable resistance value?
A carbon composition resistor is an example of what type of resistor?
questions.explain: It's a fixed resistor that restricts current to a certain level.

questions.q: What does the resistance of a thermistor depend on?
questions.explain: The word 'thermistor' is a portmanteau of 'thermal' and 'resistor.'

questions.q: What does EIA stand for in resistor color coding?
What color represents the digit 0 in the resistor color code?
Which color in the resistor color code indicates a tolerance of ±5%?
questions.explain: Gold = ±5%, Silver = ±10%.

questions.q: How many holes are vertically connected in a single row on a breadboard's terminal strip?
questions.explain: Each set of 5 vertically connected holes lets you plug in component leads.

questions.q: What is the long horizontal row on the edge of a breadboard called?
What is the purpose of the trench (center divider) on a breadboard?
choices: To separate the two halves of terminal strips so DIP chips don't bridge them

questions.q: What provides the electrical energy in a circuit?
In which circuit type is there only one current path?
If one bulb blows in a series circuit, what happens?
questions.explain: A series circuit has only one path for current.

questions.q: In a parallel circuit, what happens if one bulb blows?
questions.explain: Parallel circuits have multiple paths for current.

questions.q: What component emits light when current flows through it?
questions.explain: LED = Light Emitting Diode.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of jumper wires?
choices: To provide electrical connections between components

questions.q: Which type of jumper wire has a male pin on one end and a female socket on the other?
Electronic component that limits or controls the flow of electric current.
Component whose resistance changes with temperature.
Component that temporarily stores electrical energy in a static electric field.
A solderless board used to build and test circuits without soldering.
The two long horizontal rows on a breadboard marked with red and blue lines.
Electronic component that emits light when current passes through it.
Type of circuit where all components share a single current path.
Type of circuit that has two or more paths for current to flow.
Flexible wires used to connect components on a breadboard.
The unit of resistance.
questions.explain: Symbol is Ω.

questions.q: Name the 4 basic parts of an electric circuit.
questions.explain: Power source → conductors → load → switch.

questions.q: List the 3 types of jumper wire ends available.
questions.explain: Abbreviated as M-M, M-F, and F-F.

questions.q: What are the 2 types of resistors based on adjustability?
List the 4 bands on a color-coded resistor in order (left to right).
questions.explain: Colors represent the digit, multiplier, and tolerance per EIA standard.

Which Arduino IDE menu adds a library to your sketch?

quizzes.title: BrainError — Code Challenges (Units 1–10)
quizzes.subject: Programming
quizzes.description: 38 hands-on ESP32 code challenges: fill-in-the-blanks, find-the-bug, fix-the-syntax, and arrange-the-lines. Covers pins, buttons, LCD I2C, ultrasonic, servos, and 7-segment displays.

questions.title: Blink setup — Pin modes
questions.prompt: Complete the setup() so the button is INPUT and the LED is OUTPUT.
questions.explain: INPUT reads signals; OUTPUT drives devices.

questions.title: Reading a button and driving an LED
questions.prompt: Fill in the missing function calls and state constants.
questions.explain: digitalRead returns the state; digitalWrite sets it.

questions.title: Serial monitor basics
questions.prompt: Complete the code so the ESP32 prints 'Hello' every second.
questions.explain: Serial.begin starts serial comm; println sends a line; delay pauses in milliseconds.

questions.title: Analog sensor read
questions.prompt: Complete the analog reading of a sensor connected to pin 34.
questions.explain: analogRead returns 0–4095 on the ESP32 (12-bit ADC).

questions.title: LDR-based automatic light
questions.prompt: Complete the logic so the LED turns ON in the dark.
questions.explain: Low light value means darkness → turn LED on.

questions.title: Ultrasonic pulse send
questions.prompt: Complete the TRIG pulse and ECHO reading.
questions.explain: TRIG must be HIGH for 10 microseconds to send a pulse.

questions.title: Servo position sweep
questions.prompt: Complete the servo sweep from 0 to 180 degrees.
questions.explain: attach() binds the pin; write() moves the servo to an angle.

questions.title: LCD I2C initialization
questions.prompt: Complete the LCD I2C setup with address 0x27 and 16 columns × 2 rows.
questions.explain: I2C address, columns, rows; init() wakes it up.

questions.title: LCD print on line 2
questions.prompt: Print 'Ready' on the second line of the LCD.
questions.explain: setCursor(col, row) — row 1 is the second line.

questions.title: 7-segment digit display (Common Cathode)
questions.prompt: Turn on the correct segments to display the digit '1' on a Common Cathode display.
questions.explain: Common Cathode: HIGH turns a segment ON; only b and c are needed for '1'.

questions.title: Pin mode for I2C
questions.prompt: Complete the Wire.begin() call with the ESP32 default I2C pins.
questions.explain: GPIO 21 = SDA, GPIO 22 = SCL on the ESP32.

questions.title: Ultrasonic distance calculation
questions.prompt: Complete the distance formula (cm = duration / 58) and print it.
questions.explain: Sound travels 1 cm in ~29 µs, and the echo round-trips, so divide by 58.

questions.title: Assignment vs comparison
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: `=` assigns; `==` compares. Use `==` inside if.

questions.title: Missing pin mode
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: To write to an LED you need OUTPUT, not INPUT.

questions.title: Wrong digital function
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: digitalWrite sets a state; digitalRead reads it.

questions.title: Serial not initialized
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: You must call Serial.begin() in setup() before using Serial.println().

questions.title: TRIG pulse too long
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: The TRIG pulse must be exactly 10 microseconds for HC-SR04.

questions.title: Forgetting to attach the servo
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: Servos use attach(), not pinMode().

questions.title: LCD not initialized
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: You must call lcd.init() before using the display.

questions.title: 7-segment segment order
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: To show '0', the middle segment (g) must be OFF.

questions.title: Missing semicolon in loop
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: Every statement in C/C++ must end with a semicolon.

questions.title: I2C pins swapped
questions.prompt: Click the buggy line, then type the corrected line.
questions.explain: Wire.begin(SDA, SCL) — SDA is GPIO 21, SCL is GPIO 22.

questions.title: Missing semicolon
questions.prompt: The code below has a syntax error. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: Every statement needs a semicolon at the end.

questions.title: Missing closing brace
questions.prompt: The code below has a syntax error. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: Every opening { needs a matching }.

questions.title: Missing include
questions.prompt: The code uses Servo but doesn't include the library. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: You must #include <Servo.h> before using the Servo class.

questions.title: Capitalization matters
questions.prompt: The function name is misspelled. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: Function names are case-sensitive. Use pinMode with capital M.

questions.title: Missing opening paren
questions.prompt: Fix the syntax error in the digitalWrite call.
questions.explain: Every function call needs a matching pair of parentheses.

questions.title: Wrong assignment symbol for analog pin
questions.prompt: The code uses = instead of == in a condition. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: `=` assigns; `==` compares. Use `==` inside if.

questions.title: Extra semicolon after for
questions.prompt: The for loop has an extra semicolon. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: A stray semicolon after for() ends the loop early.

questions.title: Missing library include for LCD
questions.prompt: The code uses LiquidCrystal_I2C but doesn't include the library. Type the corrected code.
questions.explain: Include both Wire.h and LiquidCrystal_I2C.h.

questions.title: Blink the LED
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to blink an LED on pin 2.
questions.explain: setup() runs once, then loop() repeats forever.

questions.title: Button controls LED
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order so a button on pin 4 controls an LED on pin 2.
questions.explain: Read the button, then conditionally drive the LED.

questions.title: Serial hello
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to print 'Hello' every second.
questions.explain: Serial.begin first, then print + delay.

questions.title: Ultrasonic distance reading
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to read distance with an HC-SR04.
questions.explain: Reset TRIG, pulse it, read ECHO, calculate distance.

questions.title: Servo sweep
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to sweep a servo from 0° to 180°.
questions.explain: attach the servo, then sweep with a for loop.

questions.title: LCD I2C setup and print
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to initialize and print to an LCD I2C.
questions.explain: Initialize, turn on backlight, move cursor, then print.

questions.title: LDR automatic light
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order for an LDR-based automatic light.
questions.explain: Read analog value, then turn LED on if it's dark.

questions.title: 7-segment show '1' on Common Cathode
questions.prompt: Put the lines in the correct order to display the digit '1' on a Common Cathode 7-segment display.
questions.explain: Set all segments as OUTPUT in setup, then turn on only b and c for '1'.
